doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Tunes called at the loft jam sessions
summary: Standards like 'I Remember You' and Rollins originals formed the repertoire.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: What kind of tunes would they call at those things?

Well I remember we used to play “I Remember You,” that was a hip standard of the time, and “Have You Met Miss Jones,” some — I mean the repertoire that I enjoyed playing was the song bag, the American Songbook tunes. I love that. But then of course we were into the originals, like the Sonny Rollins originals, “Pent Up House” and I forget the titles but we all knew them. And standards. You know in those days repertoire was so important, especially to a piano player you know.
